title: The City That Ran Out of Water #shorts

lines.text: What if an entire city ran out of water? In twenty eighteen, Cape Town was ninety days away from finding out.
Four million people. Taps about to go dry. They even named the day: Day Zero.
The plan? Two hundred guarded water points, and just twenty-five litres per person. About two and a half buckets, for everything.
Before that, everyone got fifty litres. Two-minute showers. Pools banned. Fountains off.
The date kept moving. April. Then May.
Then the whole city cut its water use, and Day Zero never came.
A year later, the dams were over eighty percent full. So what happens when an entire city runs out of water? Four million people learn to shower in two minutes.

sources: https://www.engineeringnews.co.za/article/cape-town-cuts-water-allowance-to-daily-50-litres-as-day-zero-nears-2018-01-18 (50 L limit down from 87 L, Day Zero predicted April 21, ~200 points of distribution, 25 L per person, ~4 million people)
https://phys.org/news/2018-02-cape-town-drought-day.amp (date moved to May 11, ~200 collection points guarded, 25 L allocation, 50 L target from 87 L)

https://weforum.org/agenda/2019/08/cape-town-was-90-days-away-from-running-out-of-water-heres-how-it-averted-the-crisis (90 days from shutoff at peak, 50 L cap, two-minute showers, pools/fountains banned, Day Zero never came, dams over 80% a year later)

facts.limit: 50 L per person per day (down from 87 L) from 1 Feb 2018
facts.dayzero_plan: about 200 collection points, 25 L per person per day
facts.dates: predicted April 21, later May 11, never happened
facts.after: dams over 80% full a year later
